referenceDna.annotatedDescription: The page opens with a compact utility header and a two-part promise: a saturated color field holds short care copy and consultation or phone actions while a human-scale care photograph occupies the adjacent half. A trust and award strip follows, then a centered care introduction and a six-item service index. Later chapters alternate service imagery with an about story, family decision support, review content, film previews, specialist topics, award marks, and news. A strong closing action band leads into a dense multi-column footer. Mobile stacks the promise and image, converts the service grid into a vertical list, and carries the same chapter order through to the footer. Transfer only the sequence and conversion placements. The original is a branded homecare provider, and its people, proof, claims, exact colors, words, and assets are not client material.

acceptanceChecks: The opening identifies the care service and presents one primary conversation action with a useful secondary contact option.
Service choices and later support chapters have distinct rhythm instead of repeating one card pattern.
The mobile layout preserves the opening action, scannable service rows, dignified image crops, and footer access.
Any review, award, location, credential, staff identity, care outcome, or availability claim is supplied by the client before use.
No source identity, original photography, exact copy, or branded proof appears in the generated site.

review.scope: official-source match, paired full-page captures, prompt, requester attestation, and rendered visual review
review.notes: Both existing captures show the official Kingsway Care homepage from promise through footer. PNG pixel dimensions were read from the image headers: desktop 1440x6934 and mobile 390x11150. The original capture date and viewport heights were not embedded in the PNGs; the manifest records standard comparison viewport heights. Low-information source patterns such as repeated tiles, brand colors, reviews, awards, and people are explicitly excluded from transfer.
